sections.bodyMarkdown:
Delta Electronics (台達電子, TWSE: 2308) is the **world's #1 maker of switching power supplies** and a diversified **power-electronics** leader — spanning power management, **data-center power and cooling**, EV powertrain and charging, industrial automation, building automation and energy/renewables. Founded in 1971 by **Bruce Cheng (鄭崇華)** as a 15-person maker of TV components, it has grown into a multinational with revenue around **NT$700bn a year** and roughly **50% global share** of PC power components. It is now run by the second generation (chairman Ping Cheng / 鄭平).

Unlike the cyclical and commodity names elsewhere in this set, Delta is a **genuine quality-growth compounder** — and, importantly, one that has been *growing into* its valuation rather than merely re-rating on hope. Earnings have nearly doubled — **EPS from NT$12.58 (FY2022) to NT$23.14 (FY2025)** — while **gross margin rose from 28.8% to 37%** and ROE reached **~22%**, propelled by the **AI-data-center power-and-cooling boom** (high-wattage server power supplies and liquid cooling). This is real, high-quality growth with **expanding** margins.

The catch — and the dominant risk — is the **valuation**. At ~**NT$2,150** the stock trades on a **P/E of ~79× and P/B of ~18.6×**, with a token 0.54% yield. Even crediting the genuine growth and the AI catalyst, that multiple **prices in sustained hypergrowth**, leaving little room for disappointment. Delta's quality is not in question; its price is the question.

Delta Electronics was founded on **4 April 1971** by **Bruce Cheng (鄭崇華)**, who left TRW and put up about NT$300,000 to start a **15-person factory** in Xinzhuang making television components. From those modest beginnings, Cheng built one of Taiwan's most admired industrial companies — guided throughout by a conviction that **energy efficiency** would become a defining global need, a philosophy that shaped Delta into a leader in power conversion and an early, genuine ESG champion.

Delta's strategic arc is one of **disciplined diversification from a core competence in power**. From TV parts it moved into **switching power supplies** — becoming the global #1 — and then expanded methodically into **power management, thermal/cooling, industrial automation, EV powertrain and charging, building automation, and renewable energy and storage**, supplemented by acquisitions (Norway's **Eltek**, surveillance/projection brand **Vivotek/Vivitek**). The common thread is **converting and managing electrical power efficiently** across ever more applications.

Bruce Cheng retired from day-to-day leadership in 2012, remaining founder and honorary chairman and continuing to champion Delta's environmental mission; the company passed to professional and **second-generation family** leadership (chairman Ping Cheng / 鄭平). The most recent chapter — Delta as an **"invisible champion of the AI era,"** supplying the power and cooling that AI data centers demand — is the latest expression of the same 50-year bet on power and efficiency.

- **1971** — Founded (4 April) by Bruce Cheng (鄭崇華) as a 15-person maker of TV components in Xinzhuang.
- **1980s** — Becomes the world's #1 in **switching power supplies**; **lists on the TWSE in 1988**.
- **1990s–2010s** — Diversifies into power management, thermal, industrial automation, EV and building automation; acquires Eltek (Norway), Vivotek and others; builds a multinational footprint.
- **2012** — Founder Bruce Cheng retires from day-to-day leadership; professional/second-generation management takes over.
- **FY2022–FY2024** — Steady growth (EPS ~NT$12.6–13.6) with gross margin rising from ~29% toward ~32%.
- **FY2025** — **AI-data-center power-and-cooling boom**: EPS jumps to **NT$23.14**, gross margin ~34%; shares re-rate sharply.
- **2026Q1** — EPS NT$7.91 on a 37% gross margin and ~22% ROE; stock ~NT$2,150 (P/E ~79×).

Delta is a mature, listed industrial leader — **not a startup** — and has grown through a disciplined mix of **retained earnings, acquisitions and modest debt**, the financing of a quality compounder rather than a leveraged or speculative one.

- **A solid, moderately-levered balance sheet.** A **47.8% debt ratio** (2026Q1) on NT$684bn of assets, against NT$357bn of equity and **~NT$161bn of cash** — comfortable for a global manufacturer that funds heavy R&D and capacity for power and cooling.
- **Strong, growing cash generation.** Operating cash flow runs solidly positive (~NT$19.9bn in 2026Q1), funding both investment and dividends.
- **A growing but low-yielding dividend.** Cash dividends (FinMind, by fiscal year) have risen with earnings: **FY2020 NT$5.5, FY2021 NT$5.5, FY2022 NT$9.84, FY2023 NT$6.43, FY2024 NT$7.0, FY2025 NT$11.6** — but the yield is just **0.54%**, because the share price has climbed far faster than the payout. Delta is a growth stock, not an income one.

The financing story is therefore that of a **well-capitalized quality manufacturer reinvesting for secular growth** (AI power, EV, automation, energy). The balance sheet is not the risk; what investors are really buying is **future growth at a very high price**, funded by a company well-equipped to pursue it.

**Stance: a world-class power-electronics compounder with a genuine, large AI catalyst and expanding margins — but priced at an extreme premium that demands the hypergrowth continues.**

The bull case:

1. **Real, high-quality growth.** EPS nearly doubled (NT$12.58 → NT$23.14) with **rising** gross margins (28.8% → 37%) and ~22% ROE — growth *with* improving profitability, not just volume.
2. **A large AI-power catalyst plus secular platforms.** Delta is a key supplier of **AI-data-center power and liquid cooling**, on top of structural growth in **EV, industrial automation and energy** — multiple electrification tailwinds.
3. **Quality and moat.** World #1 in switching power supplies (~50% PC power share), deep energy-efficiency technology, scale, brand and an ESG-leading reputation.

The dominant counter-argument is **valuation**:

- **~79× P/E and ~18.6× P/B** price in **sustained hypergrowth**; even genuine quality leaves little margin for error at that multiple.
- **AI-power demand could normalize**, and the gold rush is drawing competition (other power and cooling suppliers) that could pressure the recent margin gains.
- **FX and cyclicality** in parts of the portfolio add variability; a high-multiple stock is vulnerable to any growth wobble.

A **quality-growth-at-a-high-price** thesis — more justified than a pure momentum name, but where the **price, not the business, is the risk.**

Delta makes money by **converting and managing electrical power efficiently** across a broad and deepening set of applications — the unifying competence behind a diverse portfolio:

- **Power electronics (the core).** Switching power supplies (world #1) and power-management products — including, crucially, **high-wattage power supplies and liquid cooling for AI data centers**, the segment driving the current surge.
- **Mobility and automation.** **EV powertrain, onboard chargers and charging infrastructure**, plus **industrial automation** (drives, motors, robotics) — large secular-growth platforms.
- **Infrastructure and energy.** Building automation, renewable energy, and energy-storage systems.

The economics are those of a **high-value, R&D-intensive manufacturer**: gross margins in the mid-30s% and rising, lifted as the mix shifts toward **higher-value AI-power, EV and automation** products and away from commoditized basics. The profit lever is **energy-efficiency technology leadership** applied to whichever electrification wave is growing fastest — today, AI-data-center power and cooling. Delta's durable advantage is that virtually every secular trend it serves (AI compute, EVs, automation, decarbonization) **needs more efficient power conversion** — and Delta is the scale leader in providing it.

Delta competes across **power electronics, data-center power/cooling, EV power and industrial automation** — a set of large, growing markets unified by **electrification and efficiency**. In its core of **switching power supplies it is the global #1** (with peers such as Lite-On and Chicony); in **data-center power and thermal** it competes with the likes of **Vertiv** and others as AI demand surges; in **automation** it faces global majors (Siemens, Mitsubishi, etc.); in **EV power** a broad and growing field.

Delta's moat is **genuine but contested**:

- **Scale and efficiency technology** — decades of power-conversion expertise and the world's leading switching-power-supply position.
- **Breadth and integration** — the ability to serve power, cooling, automation and EV from one platform.
- **Brand, quality and ESG reputation** that win blue-chip customers.

The competitive risk is precisely the **AI-power gold rush**: the surge in data-center power and cooling demand that is lifting Delta's margins is also **attracting capacity and competition**, which over time could compress the very margin gains the stock is celebrating. Delta is a real leader riding powerful secular tailwinds — but it operates in **competitive, partly cyclical markets**, and its current premium valuation assumes it keeps winning more than its rivals for years.

**Strengths**
- World #1 in switching power supplies (~50% PC power share); deep energy-efficiency technology.
- Genuine quality growth — EPS nearly doubled with **rising** margins (28.8% → 37%), ROE ~22%.
- Large AI-data-center power/cooling catalyst plus EV, automation and energy platforms; strong balance sheet.

**Weaknesses**
- **Extreme valuation** (P/E ~79×, P/B ~18.6×) prices in sustained hypergrowth.
- Export-heavy → FX exposure; parts of the portfolio are cyclical.
- Token 0.54% yield — purely a growth stock.

**Opportunities**
- AI-data-center power and liquid cooling content growth; EV/automation/energy electrification.
- Continued mix-driven margin expansion.

**Threats**
- AI-power demand normalization and rising competition (power/cooling suppliers) compressing margins.
- A high-multiple stock vulnerable to any growth disappointment.
- Cyclical and FX headwinds.

- **Valuation / de-rating.** The dominant risk: at ~79× earnings, even a high-quality grower has little room for error — any growth or margin disappointment could trigger a sharp de-rating.
- **AI-power normalization and competition.** The AI-data-center power/cooling surge driving today's margins is attracting competition and capacity that could erode the gains.
- **Cyclicality in segments.** Industrial automation, EV and consumer-related power demand are cyclical and can soften.
- **FX exposure.** As an export-oriented multinational, NT$/US$ and other currency moves affect reported results.
- **Execution.** Sustaining margin expansion and growth across a broad portfolio requires continued flawless execution to justify the multiple.

Delta's next two to three years will test whether a genuinely high-quality grower can **keep growing fast enough to justify an exceptional valuation**. The axes to watch:

- **AI-data-center power and cooling.** The current growth engine — whether high-wattage server power and liquid-cooling demand stays strong and Delta holds share and margin as competition arrives.
- **Margin trajectory.** Whether the gross margin keeps climbing (now ~37%) on mix shift toward AI/EV/automation, or plateaus — the key to justifying the multiple.
- **EV, automation and energy.** Execution across the other electrification platforms that diversify the growth beyond AI servers.
- **Growth vs the multiple.** Ultimately, whether earnings growth keeps pace with — or outruns — the ~79× P/E, or whether the valuation normalizes.

Bottom line: Delta is a **genuine, world-class power-electronics compounder** with real, margin-expanding growth and a large AI-power catalyst — the rare quality-growth name in this set. But it trades at an **extreme premium (P/E ~79×, P/B ~18.6×)** that prices in years of sustained hypergrowth. Judge it on whether the AI-power and electrification growth keeps compounding fast enough to grow into that price — the business is excellent; the **valuation is the risk.**
